title: Kashmir Marketplace
tagline: A modern e-commerce platform for Kashmir's artisans
description: A full-stack e-commerce application connecting Kashmir's traditional artisans with buyers worldwide, featuring real-time inventory management and secure payments.
longDescription: Kashmir Marketplace was built to solve a real problem — local artisans in Kashmir had no digital platform to reach global buyers. I designed and built the entire full-stack solution using Next.js for the frontend and Node.js/MongoDB for the backend. The platform supports multiple sellers, real-time inventory, and a clean browsing experience that puts the craftsmanship front and centre.
highlights: Multi-vendor support with individual seller dashboards
Real-time inventory tracking and order management
challenges: Building a multi-vendor system with complex data relationships while keeping the UI intuitive for non-technical artisans.
outcome: Platform launched with 20+ artisans onboarded in the first month.

title: Nature Captures
tagline: A platform for photographers to showcase their work
description: A photography showcase platform where photographers can create profiles, upload high-resolution photos, and build an audience.
longDescription: Nature Captures was my first serious full-stack project — a platform for photographers to share their work. Users can create accounts, upload photos with metadata, and browse a curated feed. I focused heavily on performance, using lazy loading and optimised image delivery to keep load times fast even with large, high-resolution images.
highlights: Responsive photo grid with masonry layout
Full-screen image viewer with keyboard navigation
challenges: Achieving fast page loads with large, high-resolution images while keeping the design elegant and distraction-free.
outcome: Clean, minimal photography showcase with excellent performance scores.

title: Simon's Game
tagline: Classic memory game — how far can you go?
description: An interactive browser-based implementation of the classic Simon memory game with increasing difficulty levels and sound effects.
longDescription: A faithful recreation of the classic Simon memory game, built to sharpen my JavaScript and DOM manipulation skills. The game generates increasingly complex colour sequences that the player must repeat. I added keyboard support and sound synthesis using the Web Audio API for a complete, accessible experience.
highlights: Multi-level difficulty with no upper limit
Sound effects via Web Audio API (no assets needed)
challenges: Synthesising different tones for each button using only the Web Audio API without loading external sound files.
outcome: Engaging game with smooth animations and audio feedback.

title: Drum Kit
tagline: Play beats in the browser with keyboard or touch
description: A fully interactive browser-based drum kit that responds to keyboard keypresses and touch events with realistic sound synthesis.
longDescription: Drum Kit turns your keyboard into a percussion instrument. Each key maps to a different drum sound, with visual feedback on keypress. I built this to explore the Web Audio API and CSS transitions — combining real-time audio with smooth UI animations.
highlights: Real-time keyboard input with zero latency
CSS press animations on each drum pad
challenges: Minimising audio latency so drum hits feel immediate and responsive.
outcome: Fun, responsive drum pad that works on both desktop and mobile.

title: Dice Roll
description: A clean two-player dice rolling app with animated dice faces and instant winner declaration.
longDescription: A simple but polished two-player dice roller. I focused on making the UI feel physical — dice have realistic face layouts and a shake animation on roll. Built as an early JavaScript project that helped cement my understanding of DOM manipulation and random number generation.
highlights: Animated dice roll with CSS shake effect
challenges: Making the dice faces look visually accurate using only CSS and HTML.
outcome: Clean, reusable dice component with smooth animations.

title: Shooting Balls
description: A canvas-based shooting game where the player must shoot incoming balls before they reach the shooter.
longDescription: Shooting Balls is a fast-paced HTML5 canvas game I built to explore game loop architecture and collision detection. The difficulty scales as the game progresses — balls spawn faster and from random angles. I implemented smooth 60fps rendering using requestAnimationFrame and pure canvas 2D APIs.
highlights: Score tracking and high score persistence
challenges: Implementing accurate collision detection that feels fair to the player at high ball speeds.
outcome: Engaging game that runs smoothly across all modern browsers.
